newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra to seek U.S. nod for ulcer mix.
newsitem.headline: Astra to seek U.S. nod for ulcer mix.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra said on Monday it would shortly seek approval in the U.S. for an ulcer treatment with a triple combination of its blockbuster anti-ulcer agent Losec and antibiotics.
Astra is lagging behind rival drug Prevacid (Lansoprazole), that was recently approved for use as a two-week triple treatment (ulcer drug and two antibiotics).
"Astra Merck is busy seeking approval," Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters.
"It is a shame we are not first but you must remember that it is a rather small market, at the most five to 10 percent of the global ulcer market."
Ternby said Astra was first in the U.S. with the first type of combination treatment that mixes antibiotics with Losec.
The combination treatment gets rid of the helicobacter pylori, the bacteria that causes ulcers.
Astra received approval for its double treatment in the U.S. almost a year ago.
In Europe the company has progressed further and a week's triple treatment is approved in most countries.
"A week's treatment seems to be the most effective. After the treatment 95 percent of patients are free of bacteria," Ternby said.
